headline: Foreign investors pulled about 15 billion dollars out of South Korean stocks in a month, mostly from the two big AI memory-chip makers.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: hard exchange data on a key AI supply-chain market, with signs the selling is easing.
importance_line: South Korean savers and pension holders saw the biggest foreign retreat from their chip champions in years while global rates rose and the Iran conflict dragged on, though early October flows suggest the exit may be slowing rather than deepening.
summary: The Korea Herald reports, citing Korea Exchange and Yonhap Infomax data, that foreign investors sold a net 20.3 trillion won, about 15.1 billion dollars, of Kospi shares between 1 Sep and 2 Oct, with SK hynix and Samsung Electronics, the two memory-chip makers at the heart of AI hardware, accounting for most of it and foreign ownership of SK hynix falling to its lowest since May 2023. Analysts blame profit-taking after this year's chip rally, rising interest rates and the US-Iran conflict, and now watch Samsung's preliminary results around 8 Oct for signs the money returns.
